passage:
A school survey asked students how they traveled to school. The results showed that almost no one walked.
The principal was surprised because she saw many walkers every morning. Later, they found the problem: the online form allowed students to choose only one answer. Students who walked to a bus stop chose "bus."
The survey was corrected and repeated. This time, walking appeared much more often.
The math teacher used the mistake as a lesson. Data can look exact and still be misleading if the question is poorly designed.
Numbers deserve respect, but not blind trust. Before using data to make decisions, people must check how the data was collected.
